newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes chairman says EMU should not be delayed.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes chairman says EMU should not be delayed.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz AG chairman Helmut Werner said European nations should not delay the planned 1999 launch of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and that the project will protect jobs, a German magazine reported on Wednesday.
Werner told Stern magazine that a delay in plans for EMU would endanger the credibility of the planned future currency, the Euro.
A summary of the article was released to the press ahead of the magazine's publication on Thursday.
"I can not imagine a second successful attempt," Werner was quoted by the magazine as saying. "The whole project would be delayed indefinitely."
Werner said monetary union would protect productivity gains Mercedes has made and make the company less dependent on foreign exchange market fluctuations.
The Mercedes boss, who has spoken out in the past in favour of monetary union, added that starting EMU with a small number of countries would offer advantages.
"A hard core of countries would make others more ambitious to join as quickly as possible," he said.
